_note: Every threshold the backend uses. api/ reads its numbers from here and nowhere else. type 'safety fact' = a published real-world limit (source + url, checked on the publisher's own page unless verified is false). type 'design choice' = our own tuning, with a one-line reason. op is how a reading is compared with value: a reading 'crosses' the limit when (reading op value) is true.

water_tds_max_ppm.source: WHO, Total dissolved solids in drinking-water (background document, 2003)
water_tds_max_ppm.note: WHO: 'Water containing TDS concentrations below 1000 mg/litre is usually acceptable to consumers'. WHO sets no health-based TDS value; this is an acceptability limit, and a sudden rise means the supply changed. 1 mg/litre = 1 ppm in water.

water_turbidity_max_ntu.source: US EPA, National Primary Drinking Water Regulations (turbidity treatment technique)
water_turbidity_max_ntu.note: EPA: state limits 'must include turbidity at no time exceeding 5 NTUs' (1 NTU for conventional or direct filtration).

air_co2_stale_ppm.source: Health Canada, Residential indoor air quality guidelines: Carbon dioxide (2021)
air_co2_stale_ppm.note: Recommended long-term exposure limit: 1,000 ppm (24-hour average). We compare single readings, so this is an early 'air going stale' warning.

air_co2_danger_ppm.source: OSHA PEL / NIOSH REL for carbon dioxide (NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards)
air_co2_danger_ppm.note: 5,000 ppm as an 8-hour time-weighted average for workers.

flood_depth_closed_cm.source: US National Weather Service, Flood Safety (Turn Around Don't Drown)
flood_depth_closed_cm.note: NWS: 'Just six inches of fast-moving water can knock over and carry off an adult.' 6 in = 15.24 cm, rounded to 15.

grid_nominal_hz.source: NERC, Reliability Guideline: Primary Frequency Control (Sept 2023)
grid_nominal_hz.note: Scheduled frequency of the North American interconnections.

grid_band_hz.source: NERC, Reliability Guideline: Primary Frequency Control (Sept 2023), Tables 4.1 and 4.5
grid_band_hz.note: Recommended maximum governor deadband: +/- 0.036 Hz. Inside this band generators do not react; outside it the grid is actively fighting a disturbance. Compared with |reading - grid_nominal_hz|.

vitals_spo2_severe_below_pct.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2), SpO2 scale 1
vitals_spo2_severe_below_pct.note: NEWS2 gives its top score (3) at SpO2 of 91% or less. Bands confirmed on NHS reproductions of the RCP chart; the RCP's own chart is a PDF linked from the url.

vitals_spo2_low_below_pct.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2), SpO2 scale 1
vitals_spo2_low_below_pct.note: NEWS2 scores 2 at SpO2 92-93%. Also the 'low oxygen' rule in the outbreak truth check.

vitals_hr_high_above_bpm.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2), pulse
vitals_hr_high_above_bpm.note: NEWS2 scores 2 at pulse 111-130 and 3 at 131 or more.

vitals_hr_low_below_bpm.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2), pulse
vitals_hr_low_below_bpm.note: NEWS2 scores 3 at pulse 40 or less.

vitals_fever_above_c.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2), temperature
vitals_fever_above_c.note: NEWS2 starts scoring at 38.1 C (band 38.1-39.0 scores 1, 39.1 or more scores 2).

vitals_spo2_healthy_min_pct.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2)
vitals_spo2_healthy_min_pct.note: First-wave health check. NEWS2 scores 0 only at SpO2 of 96% or more (scale 1).

vitals_hr_healthy_min_bpm.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2)
vitals_hr_healthy_min_bpm.note: First-wave health check. NEWS2 scores 0 for pulse 51-90.

vitals_hr_healthy_max_bpm.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2)
vitals_hr_healthy_max_bpm.note: First-wave health check. NEWS2 scores 0 for pulse 51-90.

vitals_temp_healthy_min_c.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2)
vitals_temp_healthy_min_c.note: First-wave health check. NEWS2 scores 0 for temperature 36.1-38.0 C.

vitals_temp_healthy_max_c.source: Royal College of Physicians, National Early Warning Score (NEWS2)
vitals_temp_healthy_max_c.note: First-wave health check. NEWS2 scores 0 for temperature 36.1-38.0 C.

surface_radiation_domes_usv_h.source: IAEA, Operational Intervention Levels for Reactor Emergencies (EPR-NPP-OILs 2017), OIL3
surface_radiation_domes_usv_h.note: OIL3 default: 1 µSv/h above background at 1 m above ground. Above it, local produce, milk and rainwater are not to be consumed, so people need a sealed habitat with its own supplies. We compare the raw scout reading (background not subtracted, which errs on the safe side).

surface_radiation_stay_usv_h.source: IAEA, Operational Intervention Levels for Reactor Emergencies (EPR-NPP-OILs 2017), OIL2
surface_radiation_stay_usv_h.note: OIL2 default: 25 µSv/h at 1 m above ground (the value for later than 10 days after shutdown; 100 µSv/h in the first 10 days). Above it people are to be relocated: nobody should live there.

surface_co2_domes_ppm.source: OSHA PEL / NIOSH REL for carbon dioxide (NIOSH Pocket Guide to Chemical Hazards)
surface_co2_domes_ppm.note: 5,000 ppm 8-hour time-weighted average. Above it the open air is not fit for a working day.

surface_co2_stay_ppm.source: NIOSH, Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health (IDLH) value for carbon dioxide
surface_co2_stay_ppm.note: IDLH 40,000 ppm: a suit or dome leak at this level is immediately life-threatening.

surface_o2_low_pct.note: 'An atmosphere containing less than 19.5 percent oxygen by volume.'

surface_o2_high_pct.note: 'An atmosphere containing more than 23.5 percent oxygen by volume' (fire hazard).

surface_temp_domes_c.source: US National Weather Service, heat index classification: Danger (103 F and above)
surface_temp_domes_c.note: 103 F = 39.4 C: 'heat cramps or heat exhaustion likely, heat stroke possible'. NWS defines this on the heat index (temperature + humidity); the scout sends air temperature only, so this is an approximation that ignores humidity.

surface_temp_stay_c.source: US National Weather Service, heat index classification: Extreme Danger (125 F or higher)
surface_temp_stay_c.note: 125 F = 51.7 C: 'heat stroke highly likely'. Same approximation as surface_temp_domes_c.

surface_temp_cold_c.source: US National Weather Service, wind chill: frostbite in 30 minutes at -19 F
surface_temp_cold_c.note: -19 F = -28.3 C wind chill: 'exposed skin can freeze in 30 minutes'. NWS defines this on wind chill; the scout sends air temperature only, so wind is ignored.

surface_pm25_domes_ugm3.source: US EPA, Air Quality Index for PM2.5 (2024 update): Hazardous
surface_pm25_domes_ugm3.note: 24-hour PM2.5 of 225.5 µg/m3 and above is the Hazardous category (AQI 301+). We compare single readings.

firstwave_default_n.reason: A first surface party of 20 is small enough to recall quickly and large enough to cover the needed skills.

firstwave_skill_points.reason: Each needed skill a volunteer has adds 10 points, so people who cover more of what the party needs go first.

firstwave_vitals_max_age_h.reason: 'Latest vitals' must be from the last 24 hours; older readings do not prove someone is healthy today.

battery_warn_hours.reason: One sleep or work shift: enough warning to charge watches, fill water and move people before the block goes dark.

battery_rearm_margin_hours.reason: The warning can fire again only after the forecast recovers to battery_warn_hours + this margin, so watches are not spammed when the forecast hovers at the line.

forecast_points.reason: The battery slope is fitted over the latest 30 power readings: long enough to smooth noise, short enough to follow a change in drain.

forecast_grid_avg_points.reason: Grid frequency in /forecast is the mean of the latest 5 readings so one noisy sample does not flip grid_stress.

forecast_min_drain_pct_per_h.reason: A slope flatter than this counts as 'not draining', so hours_left is null instead of a huge meaningless number.

triage_base_points.reason: Every help press starts at the same score; vitals and waiting time only add to it.

triage_spo2_severe_points.reason: Very low blood oxygen is the most urgent single sign, so it adds the most.

triage_spo2_low_points.reason: Low but not critical oxygen adds half the severe weight.

triage_hr_points.reason: A very fast or very slow pulse adds less than severe oxygen loss and more than fever.

triage_fever_points.reason: Fever alone is the least urgent of the three vital signs.

triage_wait_minutes_per_point.reason: Each 5 minutes of waiting adds one point so nobody is starved at the back of the queue.

triage_wait_max_points.reason: Waiting can add at most 20 points, so a long wait never outranks a severe oxygen reading by itself.

triage_vitals_grace_s.reason: Vitals taken up to 60 s after the help press still describe that emergency.

ingest_max_body_bytes.reason: 5 MB holds a relay backlog of about 30,000 readings; anything larger is refused so one bad client cannot exhaust memory.

ingest_rate_limit_per_s.reason: No real device needs more than 20 single posts a second; a backlog sent as one array counts as one request and is never dropped. Override with the RATE_LIMIT env var.

ingest_max_future_min.reason: A reading stamped more than 5 minutes ahead of the server clock is a broken clock or a forgery, and would corrupt forecasts, so it is rejected.

ingest_min_valid_time.reason: An ESP32 with no clock sync reports 1970. Any time before 2020 is treated as 'no clock': the reading is kept, stamped with the receive time and marked time_estimated.

status_alert_window_min.reason: /status lists the alerts of the last hour: recent enough to act on, short enough to read at a glance.

status_alert_max.reason: /status returns at most the 100 newest alerts of the window so a poll every few seconds stays small; the count is always the full number.

ingest_drain_factor.reason: An oversize upload is read and discarded so the sender gets a clear 413; past 10 times the limit the connection is simply cut.

ingest_rate_table_max.reason: The rate-limit table is cleared when it holds more than 5,000 device names, so invented names cannot grow memory without bound.

feed_retry_ms.reason: Browsers are told to wait 2 s before reconnecting to /feed: quick enough to look live, slow enough not to hammer a restarting server.

feed_ping_s.reason: A comment line every 20 s keeps proxies and load balancers from closing an idle /feed connection.

truth_window_h.reason: The residents' case count covers the last 24 hours, matching a daily official bulletin.
